script.title: Why Tycho Brahe Built Uraniborg on Hven

lines: A young Danish nobleman stares up at a star that should not exist.
It is 1572. Tycho Brahe sees a brand-new star, brighter than any star or planet.
Telescopes do not exist yet.
So Tycho starts building bigger, more exact instruments to measure the sky by eye.
King Frederick the Second offers him grand castles.
Tycho does not want any of them.
He calls life at court rubbish.
He secretly plans to move to Basel.
The king hears about it and wants to keep him.
So in 1576, the king gives him a whole island, Hven, and money for an observatory.
You see, it's like doing homework in a quiet room. Nobody bumps your elbow, so every line comes out straight.
On Hven, he can work without interruptions from other people.
Tycho builds a castle called Uraniborg, packed with giant quadrants and sextants.
Almost 100 students and craftsmen work there.
The island's farmers must grow twice as much and help build it.
They take Tycho to court, and they lose.
Later, Tycho works in a second observatory underground.
His castle instruments were not steady enough.
Tycho never uses a telescope.
But his naked-eye numbers let Johannes Kepler write three laws of how planets move.

claims.claim: In 1572 Tycho noticed a completely new star brighter than any star or planet and devoted himself to ever more accurate instruments of measurement.
Tycho was the last major astronomer before the invention of the telescope, observing with the naked eye.
The king offered Tycho castles such as Hammershus or Helsingborg; Tycho declined, calling society there 'the whole rubbish', and secretly planned to move to Basel.
The King heard of Tycho's plans and, desiring to keep him, in 1576 offered him the island of Hven and funding to set up an observatory.
Hven was chosen for seclusion, letting Tycho focus on his work without interruptions from other people.
Uraniborg had quadrants, sextants and astronomical clocks; almost 100 students and artisans worked there.
Tycho required the peasants to cultivate twice as much and to labor on his castle; they took him to court and the court established his right to levy taxes and labor.
He later worked underground at Stjerneborg, where he realised his instruments in Uraniborg were not sufficiently steady.
Kepler used Tycho's data to develop his three laws of planetary motion.

cast.tycho: a 26 year old Danish nobleman with reddish blond hair, a long drooping reddish moustache, a broad scar across his forehead, a black doublet with a white ruff collar and a gold chain, 1570s

cast.kepler: a 30 year old thin German mathematician with dark hair, a short dark pointed beard, a narrow pale face and a plain black coat with a small white ruff, 1600s
